unit.title: The Imperfect Subjunctive
unit.subtitle: Wishes, hypotheticals, and reported requests in the past

grammar.title: Build it from the preterite, not the infinitive
grammar.intro: The imperfect subjunctive (imperfecto de subjuntivo) is the subjunctive for the past and for hypotheticals. Its secret is simple: don't build it from the infinitive — build it from the third-person plural preterite. Drop the -ron and add the endings. Because that preterite already carries every irregularity, this form handles even irregular verbs cleanly.

sections.heading: 3rd-person plural preterite − ron + ra endings
sections.body: Take the ellos preterite (hablaron, comieron, vivieron), remove -ron, and add these endings. The nosotros form takes a written accent:

sections.heading: Irregular verbs come along for free
sections.body: Because you start from the preterite, irregular stems are already baked in. Learn the ellos preterite and the subjunctive falls out automatically:

sections.heading: When you need it
sections.body: Use it after a past-tense main verb that triggers the subjunctive, and in hypothetical si-clauses. (An -ase form also exists — hablase — but -ara is the one to learn first.)

ex.en: I wanted you to talk to her.
If I had money, I would travel.

takeaways: Build from the 3rd-person plural preterite: drop -ron, add -ra endings.
Irregulars come from the preterite: fueron→fuera, tuvieron→tuviera, hicieron→hiciera.
Triggered by past-tense main verbs (Quería que...) and hypotheticals (Si tuviera...).

mistakes.why: Build from the preterite tuvieron, not from the infinitive tener: tuviera.
A hypothetical si-clause needs the imperfect subjunctive, not the imperfect indicative.
hacer comes from hicieron → hiciera; there is no z here.
